Prevention: Cotton leaf curl virus disease (CLCV) is transmitted by whitefly i.e.
Bemisia tabaci , so control of the vector significantly reduces the risk of disease (see yellow section).
New sources of resistance should be identified from all available germplasm.
Ensure good field sanitation and hygiene.
Management of alternate hosts including clean cultivation through weed management.
Proper rouging of the infected plants.
Monitoring: CLCV-affected cotton is done to characterize the variability of symptoms and disease perpetuation.
Upward and downward curling of leaves accompanied by small main vein thickenings on leaves.
Direct Control: At initial stage of whitefly attack, cold water spray with 1 teaspoon of detergent/tank is effective against whitefly.
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing when spraying dangerous chemicals (masks, boots, gloves…)
Do not eat or smoke when spraying chemicals.
